title: The Line of Least Expectation
sourceSection: Part V -- Unconventional (Dirty) Warfare (first teaching chapter)
keyConcepts: misperception: shape the opponent's picture by selecting which real facts to emphasize
ordinary-extraordinary: vary texture so the opponent cannot predict the next move
void: deny the opponent a concentrated target to attack
alliance: find genuine interest overlap with stronger parties
fait accompli: aggregate small moves below the opposition threshold into an irreversible position
connectingThread: All five strategies share the principle of asymmetry: the operator reshapes the field indirectly rather than confronting the opponent head-on. The suite is most valuable when the operator is weaker or when direct engagement is not the most efficient path.
reversalFlags: framing collapses if selected facts are later shown to be intentionally misleading
unpredictability becomes a pattern itself if used compulsively
void strategy requires giving up concentration and visible authority
alliance collapses when stronger party discovers manufactured overlap
fait accompli fails if opponent recognizes the pattern early and mobilizes
callbackOpportunities: Ch7 Indirection: Ch9 is the next layer beyond flank/wedge/ripening
Ch8 Negotiated Outcomes: unconventional toolkit when negotiation is not available
Ch3 Choosing Not to Fight: void is the offensive cousin of nonengagement
moralFlagNote: The ethical line between legitimate strategy and manipulation is most likely to blur in this chapter. Strategic framing vs. propaganda. Genuine alliance vs. manufactured overlap. Fait accompli vs. deception by increments. Each strategy has a legitimate form (works with real facts and genuine overlap) and a manipulative form (fabricates information or manufactures overlap). The chapter must name both explicitly.
